meta.fix_commit: php/php-src 82f8f31b16a ("Avoid state corruption via bailout", branch PHP-8.0-CVE-2026-109618-109619) - fixes both CVEs together
meta.note: 2026-10-21 rewrite: this file previously described a single-request multipart-stall heap-spray mechanism (byte offsets, FILLUNIT, 149-field spray count) derived from the leaked PoC artifact's own claims. That mechanism did not match the real fix and has been deleted, not caveated. Everything below is grounded in the actual php-src fix commit. See ANALYSIS.md for the full writeup.

vulnerability.root_cause: zend_mm_safe_error (Zend/zend_alloc.c) handled OOM/integer-overflow via zend_error_noreturn + unconditional zend_bailout() - both longjmp-based, skipping cleanup code downstream of the jump point. Fixed by replacing with a hard _exit(1), no longjmp.
vulnerability.cross_request_mechanism: A longjmp-interrupted (producer) request can skip the reset of worker-persistent globals (EG(user_error_handler), EG(exception), EG(objects_store), PG(http_globals)[], PG(modules_activated), SG(request_info).auth_user/auth_password/auth_digest/content_type_dup/current_user). A later, different (consumer) request on the SAME worker process can read these before its own init_executor()/php_request_startup() resets them.
confirmed_consumer_paths: zend_error_zstr_at - reachable via early INI diagnostics (e.g. .htaccess/php_value under mod_php)
php_session_rfc1867_callback - the session.upload_progress multipart hook; confirmed by the EOL-branch fix disabling it outright (if (!PS(rfc1867_enabled) || true))
vulnerability.producer_amplification_vector: main/rfc1867.c's multipart_buffer_headers() previously saved every header line in a multipart part unconditionally - an attacker-controlled single part with an unlimited number of headers costs far more memory inside PHP than on the wire, driving OOM cheaply. Fixed: now only saves Content-Disposition/Content-Type, skips duplicates.
vulnerability.mitigation: No complete generic configuration mitigation (per the PHP advisory). session.upload_progress.enabled=0 closes one confirmed consumer path; fatal_error_backtraces=0 (PHP 8.5 only) closes the strongest confirmed producer path. Preventing worker reuse (pm.max_requests=1 / MaxConnectionsPerChild 1) makes the cross-request consumer step structurally impossible, at a performance cost.

heap_reclaim_technique.note: Separate from the trigger: the fix also hardens how freed memory gets reclaimed. main/php_variables.c now builds $_POST/$_GET/$_COOKIE via a new array_init_singleton() (Zend/zend_hash.c's zend_new_array_singleton(), nTableSize forced to 1) instead of the default dynamically-sized array_init(). This confirms a heap-spray/reclaim step is a real part of exploitation -- it is just reached via the cross-request mechanism above, not a same-request spray at fixed byte offsets. No specific blob layout or offset table is confirmed for the real mechanism; the ones in the prior revision of this file were artifact-specific claims that do not match the fix.

reproduced_2026_10_21.note: Own lab, pre-patch PHP 8.3.6 (Ubuntu 8.3.6-0ubuntu0.24.04.12 -- the distro's default .13 build already had the fix backported despite the unchanged version string; confirmed via zend_new_array_singleton symbol presence/absence). One multipart part, 1,400,000 duplicate 5-byte header lines, 7,000,111 bytes wire.
reproduced_2026_10_21.measured_via: PHP's own memory_get_peak_usage(true) -- the metric memory_limit enforcement checks against, not an external RSS proxy (RSS sampling was flat/misleading in an earlier attempt)
reproduced_2026_10_21.memory_limit_sweep: 2M/4M/8M/16M/32M/64M/128M/256M -> hard worker crash + respawn (502, php-fpm log 'exited with code 70', new child PID). 512M/1024M -> clean 200, same worker PID before/after.
reproduced_2026_10_21.gap: Crash-and-respawn at low memory_limit is NOT the survive-with-corrupted-state CVE-2026-109619 needs. See unreproduced section.

unreproduced.note: An end-to-end RCE, or even a confirmed ASAN use-after-free, under whichever producer trigger leaves a surviving (not crashed) worker. The header-explosion OOM trigger reproduced above (see reproduced_2026_10_21) hard-crashes the worker instead of surviving with corrupted state -- it demonstrates CVE-2026-109618 convincingly but not CVE-2026-109619's cross-request consumer step. The advisory's strongest demonstrated case for that is PHP 8.5 + fatal_error_backtraces, a different producer path, untested here as of this writing. Also unconfirmed: which early-init paths beyond php_session_rfc1867_callback and zend_error_zstr_at are reachable in a default configuration. See ANALYSIS.md.

this_artifact_only._note: Literal to the one released PoC (http://jackalsyn.com/posts/phpupAssets/php-up-2026.tar.gz, sha256 0c254d547cac650bfbcb2275e30c2083737520a51a0511646f1fbb7ed60a0d63). VulnCheck independently reports that none of the public PoCs they reviewed have the correct mechanism for this CVE pair -- treat this artifact's own documented technique as unverified, not as a description of the real vulnerability. These strings remain useful only as blocklist-grade IOCs for that one tool/campaign, same caveat as before.
